grades.quote: software must execute fence or cache-control instructions to ensure specific ordering of memory accesses beyond the requirements of the assumed memory consistency model and execution environment.
grades.reason: General RISC-V memory consistency overview (RVWMO/TSO). It only mentions that fence instructions are needed for extra ordering. It doesn't describe a barrier's ordering guarantees or its control fields.

grades.quote: In addition to the above atomic sequence of operations, the `AM{SWAP/ADD}_DB.{B/H}` instruction also implements the data barrier function.
grades.reason: LoongArch passage on AM*_DB atomics. It says the _DB variants act as a data barrier: earlier accesses complete first, and later accesses wait until the atomic completes. That is a useful part of the ordering answer. It is not a dedicated barrier instruction and has no barrier control fields.
